title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

questions.broad: For high-entropy alloys used in thermal-insulation applications, what testable hypothesis could be made about an unspecified predictive approach for accurately identifying materials with low phonon thermal conductivity? The hypothesis should explain why the approach would work, predict its improvement over current predictions, define its applicability limits, identify supporting evidence, and specify a decisive experimental benchmark and outcome that would falsify it.
questions.problem_constrained: For bulk HfNbTaTiZr, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified predictive approach make to overcome the limited accuracy of available analytical predictions and their usual restriction to perfect, defect-free crystals? Address the nearly 0–200 K regime and the 300–1200 K regime, for which measurements also exist on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen; explain why the approach should improve accuracy, predict its advantage over existing analytical approaches, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a held-out conductivity benchmark and result that would falsify the hypothesis.
questions.expert_context: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

gap.evidence: Available analytical approaches to predict the phonon thermal conductivity of HEAs ... are not able to include the chemical SRO.
gap.reason: Existing predictive approaches cannot account for chemical short-range order, a structural feature known to influence thermal transport in HEAs.
